title: Power of a Lens
notes: **Definition:** $P = 1/f$, where $f$ is in metres. Units: dioptres (D).
**Convex lens:** $f$ is positive, so $P$ is positive. A +2.0 D lens has $f = 0.5\,\text{m} = 50\,\text{cm}$.
**Concave lens:** $f$ is negative, so $P$ is negative. A -4.0 D lens has $f = -0.25\,\text{m} = -25\,\text{cm}$.
**Combination in contact:** $P_{total} = P_1 + P_2 + P_3 + \ldots$. Powers add algebraically because thin lenses in contact have a combined focal length given by $1/f_{eq} = 1/f_1 + 1/f_2$.

**Optician's prescription:** a prescription of +3.0 D means a converging lens of focal length 33.3 cm for hyperopia (farsightedness); -2.5 D means a diverging lens of focal length -40 cm for myopia (nearsightedness).
